normative_action: The code-reviewer subagent performs a read-only review: Write, Edit and NotebookEdit are disallowed tools and it must not edit files.
trigger_scope: code-reviewer subagent (PR review, diff review, pre-merge review, second-pass review of completed work)
exceptions: Bash is not tool-disallowed; the no-edit duty for shell use rests on the instruction text only.

normative_action: The code-reviewer runs the preloaded code-review workflow on the requested scope and returns its report; it must not redefine review criteria — the workflow and the repository standards it loads are authoritative.
The frontend workspace lives at frontend/<Name>.Web/ (shared layout convention), separate from backend projects and docs.
exceptions: With frontend selection none no workspace exists.

normative_action: Package add/install/update commands must pin an exact version: npm/pnpm/yarn install|add|update with a registry spec that lacks an exact semver, and dotnet add package / dotnet package add|update without an exact --version (or id@version), are blocked and routed to the add-dependency workflow (version selection).
modality: MUST (PreToolUse hook: blocks before execution, exit 2, fails closed)
trigger_scope: Bash and PowerShell commands, including chains and shell wrappers (bash -c, cmd /c, powershell -Command/-EncodedCommand) up to nesting depth 3
exceptions: Local path, file:, link:, workspace:, git and URL specs count as pinned; exact prerelease versions pass the hook (prerelease avoidance is not hook-enforced); only npm, pnpm, yarn and dotnet are recognized.

normative_action: Dependency updates that name no package (npm/pnpm/yarn update|upgrade without specs, audit fix, dotnet package update without an id) are blocked before execution and routed to the add-dependency workflow, so every update goes through per-package version selection and due diligence.
modality: MUST (PreToolUse hook: blocks before execution, exit 2)
exceptions: Named updates fall under the exact-version rule (RULE-K1-0004).

normative_action: npm/pnpm/yarn install, update, remove, restore (ci, dedupe, prune) or audit-fix commands carrying --force, -f or --legacy-peer-deps are blocked as peer-dependency bypasses and routed to the add-dependency workflow (peer-dependency conflicts).
modality: MUST NOT (PreToolUse hook: blocks before execution, exit 2)
exceptions: Flag value =false is allowed; the hook blocks the flags regardless of the stated purpose; other npm verbs (e.g. cache) are not classified.

normative_action: When backend production C# files (backend/**/*.cs outside *Test/*Tests projects; deletions ignored) changed with no backend test change, the agent is reminded at Stop to confirm test coverage and probe preservation and must address the reminder or state why it does not apply before finishing.
modality: SHOULD (Stop hook: blocks stopping once per content state; reminder must be addressed or justified)
trigger_scope: Stop event in a Git work tree with working-tree changes
exceptions: Inactive outside a Git work tree; each reminder content state is reported once; a continuation triggered by the hook is never re-blocked.

normative_action: When persistence model files (Domain .cs, Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/*.cs, Infrastructure/Persistence/*DbContext.cs) changed without any development seeder change (Infrastructure/Persistence/Seeding/), the agent is reminded at Stop to confirm whether seeded entities are affected and must address it or state why it does not apply.
modality: SHOULD (Stop hook reminder, blocks stopping once per content state)
trigger_scope: Stop event in a Git work tree
exceptions: Same once-per-content-state and Git-only limits as RULE-K1-0007.

normative_action: When migration files (backend/*.Infrastructure/Persistence/Migrations/) changed, the agent is reminded at Stop to review them as source code before committing and must address it or state why it does not apply.
modality: SHOULD (Stop hook reminder, blocks stopping once per content state)
trigger_scope: Stop event in a Git work tree
exceptions: Same once-per-content-state and Git-only limits as RULE-K1-0007.

normative_action: Static capability composition: each required slot (architecture frame, persistence leaf, backend-testing leaf) has exactly one implementation (persistence with exactly one provider variant); the optional frontend slot has zero or one; selection none means no frontend workspace, no facets and a register row recording none (pointers to absent facet locations stay valid and dormant); unselected implementations are not part of the runtime.
trigger_scope: Template capability structure: .claude/capabilities, decision-register selection, template maintenance and capability replacement
why_extra_or_uncertain: No oracle policy defines the template's own capability-slot composition or cardinality; this constrains how the instruction system may be structured and changed (repo/meta), beyond ARC-020/DEP-009 which only require approval for new persistence or replacing approved technology.

normative_action: A slot implementation must provide every required item listed in its slot CONTRACT.md (architecture: role-map, dependency-direction, domain-modeling, use-case-orchestration, commit-boundary-placement, composition-root, transport-contracts, test-project-placement, not-adopted-styles, scaffold-layout, reference-check; backend-testing: framework-standard, integration-host-binding, knowledge, test-scaffold, framework-consistency-check; frontend: stack-properties, framework-standard, knowledge, workspace-scaffold, library-check; persistence: technology-boundary, commit-boundary-binding, migration-mechanism, seeding-mechanism, provider-variant, declared-properties, testing-implications, change-workflow, knowledge, enforcement).
trigger_scope: Creating or replacing a slot implementation (template maintenance, architecture-decision)
why_extra_or_uncertain: Template capability contracts are research/template structure, not V2 policy; they require e.g. deterministic reference checks, library checks and framework-consistency checks as part of any implementation, which no oracle policy demands.

normative_action: Non-slot artifacts refer to slot concerns through each slot's stable role vocabulary (architecture: Domain, Application, Infrastructure, Api, Application Service, repository contract, Unit of Work/IUnitOfWork, test projects) rather than through the selected implementation's names (leak rule).
trigger_scope: Authoring or changing instruction-system artifacts outside capability modules
exceptions: Per the leak checker: facet files listed in the module manifest, the module directory, .claude/MAP.md, project-owned files (SPECIFICATION.md, CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md, .editorconfig, Directory.Build.props, Directory.Packages.props), and the register's capability-selection block and Accepted decisions log may name the implementation.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-authoring vocabulary rule of the K1 capability design; no oracle policy restricts which technology names may appear in which instruction files.

normative_action: Frame/leaf ownership: placement (project roles, commit-boundary placement, composition, test-project placement and references) belongs to the architecture frame; technique belongs to the leaf slots (persistence, backend-testing), which declare their frame bindings with Binds:.
trigger_scope: Template content ownership during template maintenance or capability replacement
why_extra_or_uncertain: Template-structure ownership rule from the K1 capability model; the oracle prescribes no ownership location for instruction content (inventory grouping explicitly must not determine candidate structure).

normative_action: Facet locations are role-named and fixed: every implementation of a slot provides exactly the slot's listed facet locations (DEC row in the decision register, STD rule file, KNW facet, WF reference/skill, ENF facet script), file names never change with the implementation, and the backend-testing knowledge facet keeps the shared skill name dotnet-testing.
exceptions: With frontend selection none the frontend facet locations are absent.
why_extra_or_uncertain: File-naming/location rule of the template's capability design, not derived from V2 policy.

normative_action: Framework-neutral standards (rules/backend-tests/testing.md; rules/frontend/frontend.md, rules/frontend/security.md, rules/frontend/dependencies.md) stay unchanged when a slot implementation is replaced.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Change-procedure rule for the template's capability model; the oracle does not regulate how instruction files change when a technology is replaced.

normative_action: A persistence provider change is a variant change inside the persistence slot, not a new slot; replacing the persistence implementation requires every contract item, and an item the proposed implementation cannot provide (e.g. a migration mechanism) is surfaced as Blocked in the Decision Request instead of being dropped.
trigger_scope: Proposals to change the persistence provider or implementation (architecture-decision)
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-002/ARC-020 require approval for replacing approved technology, but no oracle policy requires a contract-item completeness assessment or a Blocked marking inside the Decision Request.

normative_action: Dependency-removal commands (npm/pnpm uninstall|remove|rm|r|un|unlink, yarn remove, dotnet remove package, dotnet package remove) are blocked before execution and routed to the add-dependency workflow (removal); deleting a frontend package.json is reported as a warning that dependency removals go through add-dependency.
modality: MUST (PreToolUse hook: blocks before execution, exit 2; PostToolUse warning on deleted package.json)
trigger_scope: Bash and PowerShell commands; frontend manifests
why_extra_or_uncertain: No oracle policy governs dependency removal (DEP-001..DEP-005 cover additions and updates); the hook makes every removal command fail via the shell regardless of approval.

normative_action: Every .NET project-reference change (dotnet add|remove reference, dotnet reference add|remove, or a .csproj ProjectReference edit) is a Reserved decision: it is blocked or flagged as an error unless each edge appears as `From -> To` in a dated (YYYY-MM-DD) row of the decision register's Accepted decisions or a docs/decisions record linked from such a row.
modality: MUST (Reserved; PreToolUse block for dotnet reference commands; PostToolUse error finding for .csproj edits)
trigger_scope: .NET project references in the active repository or worktree
exceptions: dotnet reference update is not classified; edges already in HEAD and reverted edits are not flagged; the Accepted decisions table ships empty.
why_extra_or_uncertain: ARC-001 already permits inward references (Api -> Application, Infrastructure -> Application) and ARC-020 requires approval for consequential changes such as new layers/projects; no oracle policy requires a recorded, dated approval for each individual reference edge, including standard inward or narrow test references.

normative_action: If the schema changes, a new migration is created (persistence-change); when persistence model files (Domain .cs, Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/*.cs, Infrastructure/Persistence/*DbContext.cs) change without any migration change, the agent is reminded at Stop to confirm whether the schema changed (a schema change is expected to come with a migration) and must address the reminder or state why it does not apply.
modality: MUST (workflow rule) / SHOULD (Stop hook reminder, blocks stopping once per content state)
trigger_scope: Stop event in a Git work tree
why_extra_or_uncertain: The oracle requires a migration only for schema-affecting CUSTOM_SETTINGS changes (PST-009) and review of generated migrations (PST-010); it contains no general duty that every model change be checked for schema impact and paired with a migration, nor a stop-time confirmation.

normative_action: Every instruction artifact is classified in the order Capability -> Kind -> Scope: capability-owned artifacts declare Capability: <slot>/<implementation> (others Capability: —); Kind (OP, DEC, STD, KNW, WF, ENF, IN) decides mechanism and location; Scope (common, backend, backend-tests, frontend, delivery, repo/meta) decides the rule directory and paths:.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-system classification scheme of the K1 design; no oracle policy dictates how instruction artifacts are classified, headed or located.

normative_action: Instruction dependency direction is WF -> KNW -> STD -> DEC -> OP and ENF -> STD/DEC; each ENF artifact declares what it conforms to on a Conforms: line directly after its header.
exceptions: Skill and agent references are routing pointers, not dependencies.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Internal dependency discipline of the instruction system, not derived from any V2 policy.

normative_action: Single owner per topic: each rule/topic lives in the artifact recorded as its owner in the map (Owns / Extend here when / Where does a topic live), new content is added at its owner, and the map is updated whenever an artifact is added, moved, or removed.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Research construction principle (one normative owner) realised as an instruction-maintenance rule; not one of the 196 V2 policies.

normative_action: Changes to the instruction system go through the user-invoked template-maintenance workflow, and changing a slot contract is a Reserved decision (rare).
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-017 makes Reserved changes approval-gated but does not make the template's own slot contracts Reserved or route instruction changes through a user-invoked maintenance workflow.

normative_action: Product, feature and task inputs may request a decision change but must not silently override engineering policy or recorded decisions; requested decision changes go through decision control (an explicit user instruction counts as approval).
trigger_scope: Conflicts between product/task inputs and policy or recorded decisions
exceptions: Requirements already in the approved specification are Decided, not Reserved.

normative_action: Capability-selection changes and other decision-register changes are Reserved decisions handled through the architecture-decision workflow.
trigger_scope: Changing selected implementations, approved stack or other register entries

normative_action: Do not introduce API versioning merely because an API exists; add it only when published compatibility or coexistence of client generations creates a concrete need.
Adopting API versioning is a Reserved decision (explicit approval required, per CLAUDE.md).
trigger_scope: Introducing API versioning in the backend
why_extra_or_uncertain: API-013 only forbids versioning without a concrete need and DEP-017 makes the package conditional; neither requires explicit approval to adopt versioning once a concrete need exists, and ARC-020's approval list does not include API versioning.

normative_action: Once an API version is relied on by external clients it must not change incompatibly in silence; a breaking contract change requires a new version or another explicitly approved compatibility strategy.
When explicit versioning is required, use one strategy consistently; URL-segment versioning unless project requirements justify another.
exceptions: project requirements may justify another strategy

normative_action: Do not create separate Domain or persistence models merely because the external API has multiple versions; isolate version-specific transport contracts at the Api boundary when practical.
Swagger/OpenAPI metadata must describe the API that actually runs (routes, important response statuses, schemas, authentication behavior); never document speculative responses.
Swagger UI is enabled in Development and exposed in other environments only when a deployment requirement explicitly justifies it.
HTTP status codes and transport response semantics belong to the Api layer; Application and Domain must not return IActionResult or ASP.NET Core status codes.
Success statuses follow actual HTTP semantics (200/201/202/204): never 200 for every outcome, 201 merely because a row was inserted internally, or 202 for already-completed work.
A successful collection query with zero matches returns 200 with an empty collection, not 404.
Use 401 for missing/failed authentication and 403 for an authenticated principal that is not permitted; returning 404 to hide a protected resource requires a deliberate, consistent security policy.
Use 409 for a valid request conflicting with current state and 412 when an explicit HTTP precondition such as If-Match fails.
Use ProblemDetails for non-validation HTTP failures and ValidationProblemDetails for request validation failures; keep machine-readable error contracts stable and safe.
Unexpected failures propagate to centralized IExceptionHandler handling; avoid repetitive catch/log/rethrow blocks.
Never expose stack traces, SQL, connection strings, internal paths, secret values or sensitive exception details in public API errors.
Log an unexpected exception once, at the boundary that handles it; never log the same exception again across repository, Application, controller and global handler.
Normal client-request cancellation must not be mapped to a generic 500 or logged as an unhandled application failure.
Represent common expected outcomes explicitly when useful (null, bool, a typed outcome); do not force a generic Result<T> pattern and do not use HTTP-named outcome categories in Application.

Use FluentValidation for explicit request/use-case validation where appropriate; validation stays at its owning boundary (transport in Api, use-case/workflow rules in Application, non-trivial invariants in Domain, external-system assumptions in Infrastructure when needed) without mechanical duplication at every layer.
Do not establish business exceptions as the default architecture or throw/catch exceptions merely to jump between normal expected branches.

The Clean Architecture frame maps backend roles to projects backend/<Name>.Domain (business concepts, independent of infrastructure/transport), backend/<Name>.Application (use-case orchestration; persistence, external-service and commit-boundary abstractions), backend/<Name>.Infrastructure (implementations of Application abstractions) and backend/<Name>.Api (HTTP entry point and composition root).

Dependencies point inward: Domain references no other application project; Application references Domain; Infrastructure references Application and Domain; Api references Application and may reference Infrastructure only for composition and registration; inner layers never depend on outer layers and Domain/Application never reference Infrastructure-specific types.
If a feature seems to need an outward reference, reconsider the abstraction boundary instead of adding the reference.
Domain stays independent of the persistence technology, ASP.NET Core, HTTP and external-service implementation concerns.

Simple domain entities by default; straightforward CRUD/workflow rules (validation rules, immutable fields, status transitions, allowed/forbidden edits) belong in Application Services and do not by themselves justify a richer model.
Move behavior into Domain only when non-trivial invariants or behavior materially benefit from domain-level encapsulation; otherwise a Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical patterns require approval.
exceptions: unless the approved specification already requires them

normative_action: Do not add factories, private setters, transition methods, Aggregate Roots, Domain Events, Specifications, Domain Services, systematic Value Objects or similar DDD constructs merely to make a simple model look domain-driven.

Application Services orchestrate use cases (Domain objects, repositories, external-service abstractions, Unit of Work); a large service is a signal to reconsider responsibilities, not an automatic reason for another pattern.
Application defines the persistence and external-service abstractions its use cases require and keeps infrastructure implementation details out.
Application must not depend on persistence-technology types/APIs (database context, entity sets, query or provider types) or ASP.NET Core transport types.
IUnitOfWork is the commit boundary of an Application use case; repositories stage changes and Application Services decide when to commit.

Repositories in one use case share the same scoped Unit of Work and persistence context; repositories are injected explicitly into consumers and IUnitOfWork must not become a repository container or service locator.
Program.cs in Api is the application composition root and may register Infrastructure implementations.

Registration stays near the owning layer: Application registers Application services, Infrastructure registers persistence and adapters, Api composes them (AddApplication(), AddInfrastructure(configuration)).
Do not duplicate equivalent DTOs across Api and Application merely to create layer-shaped types; introduce transport-specific contracts in Api when separation provides a concrete boundary benefit.
ASP.NET Core Controllers are the default HTTP entry point and stay thin: bind/validate input, invoke Application services, translate outcomes to HTTP responses.
Controllers must not contain business logic, access the database context or concrete repositories, or construct infrastructure services manually.
Constructor injection for required dependencies; avoid service-locator and property-injection patterns.
Dependency lifetimes must be valid; never capture a shorter-lived dependency inside a longer-lived service.
Cache technology stays out of Domain and infrastructure cache APIs must not leak into Application without a deliberate boundary abstraction.
Infrastructure translates remote HTTP responses into Application-facing abstractions; HttpResponseMessage and remote transport concerns must not leak into Application.
Follow the repository's conventions and .editorconfig; use modern C# when it improves clarity but do not rewrite working code solely for newer syntax.

For new C# code: file-scoped namespaces when consistent with the project; one primary top-level type per file with a matching name (small private/nested supporting types may stay with their owner); Async suffix on Task/ValueTask-returning methods unless an existing or framework contract makes it inappropriate.
No style-only rewrites outside the requested change unless explicitly asked; avoid mixing large formatting or modernization changes with functional work.

NuGet Central Package Management is mandatory: versions live in Directory.Packages.props; project PackageReference entries carry no version (central versions never duplicated in project files; a VersionOverride needs a recorded reason) and live in the narrowest project that requires the package.
trigger_scope: backend NuGet (rule loads for backend/**, Directory.*.props)

normative_action: Health checks stay cheap and deterministic and must not become business workflows or perform expensive or mutating database work.

Liveness avoids external dependencies whose unavailability could cause restart loops; readiness may depend on capabilities required to serve traffic and must reflect startup and dependency availability.
Publicly reachable health responses must not expose secrets, credentials, connection details, stack traces or unnecessary internal diagnostics.
ILogger<T> with structured message templates and stable property names; avoid string interpolation that turns structured values into opaque text.
When Serilog is configured, use the DI-integrated AddSerilog approach with provider configuration in environment-aware configuration; application code continues to depend on ILogger<T>.
Strongly typed options for structured service configuration, validated at startup when missing/invalid values prevent correct or secure operation; avoid scattered string-based IConfiguration lookups.
Production containers use an appropriate runtime image, not the SDK image for convenience, and do not switch to root merely to bypass filesystem problems.

EF Core is an Infrastructure implementation detail used fully inside Infrastructure; DbContext, DbSet<T>, EF Core APIs, EF-backed IQueryable<T> and provider-specific types must not leak into Application.
Infrastructure implements IUnitOfWork by delegating to the shared scoped AppDbContext.
No explicit transaction APIs until a concrete use case requires transaction control beyond a single SaveChangesAsync.
Development seeding is an Infrastructure/bootstrap concern and may use AppDbContext directly; it need not go through Application repositories or IUnitOfWork.

Substantial seed construction lives in a dedicated internal DbSeeder exposed through a narrow Infrastructure initialization extension — never in Program.cs, AppDbContext configuration, entity configurations or migrations.

EF Core persistence code is organised under backend/<Name>.Infrastructure/Persistence/: the DbSeeder in Persistence/Seeding/, migrations in Persistence/Migrations/, entity configurations in Persistence/Configurations/ and the DbContext file there.
modality: MUST (placement convention; enforcement reminders key on these paths)
why_extra_or_uncertain: PST-003 requires a dedicated internal seeder surface and ARC-019 keeps EF Core in Infrastructure, but no oracle policy fixes folder paths; the candidate binds concrete folders and its Stop-hook reminders only recognise these paths.

normative_action: The development seeder must not call Database.Migrate(), EnsureCreated() or otherwise create/upgrade the schema; migrations are applied separately before seeding.

appsettings.Development.json provides a usable local Development connection string when it contains no secret credentials; credential-bearing local values come from user-secrets or another approved local secret mechanism.

Specific repository interfaces represent actual cohesive Application persistence needs, not table-mirroring generic CRUD contracts; repository interfaces are defined in Application and implemented in Infrastructure.

Repository interfaces must not expose IQueryable<T>, database-context or entity-set types, query expressions or provider-specific types; query construction stays in Infrastructure; return materialized entities, collections, projections or explicit result models.
Application must not depend on IGenericRepository<T> or another generic CRUD contract; a generic repository/base class may exist only as an Infrastructure detail that removes real duplication.
exceptions: Infrastructure-only generic base removing real duplication

normative_action: Database access is parameterized; never build SQL by concatenating untrusted input (raw SQL, micro-ORMs, ADO.NET included).
An empty Development database receives a small deterministic representative seed dataset covering the main meaningful states and relationships.
Automatic seeding runs only in Development, never automatically in Production; the development seeder is not test setup and tests own their setup.

When representative data already exists leave it unchanged; never use the seeder for automatic synchronization, repair, upgrade, overwrite or recreation of an existing Development database (developers recreate local databases explicitly).
Seed entities preserve current Domain invariants and valid relationships; prefer readable deterministic examples over exhaustive or random combinations.
Clear, correct code first; no specialized optimization without a concrete reason, and measurement/profiling evidence for non-trivial optimizations.
Compiled queries, ValueTask, pooling, custom serialization, aggressive caching and raw SQL for performance only for a measured or clearly demonstrated need.
Use async APIs for asynchronous I/O and never block them with .Result, .Wait() or similar sync-over-async patterns.
Propagate CancellationToken through asynchronous operations when cancellation is meaningful; do not add cancellation parameters to purely synchronous code without a use case.
TimeProvider for logic depending on the current clock that needs deterministic tests; do not mechanically replace explicit or stored timestamps.
Filter and project in the database when practical, avoid unnecessary round trips, over-fetching and N+1, and paginate potentially large result sets.
Never create and dispose a new HttpClient per request; use IHttpClientFactory or another appropriate long-lived client strategy.
External I/O calls have a bounded execution time appropriate to the operation; avoid overlapping timeout mechanisms with unclear combined behavior.
Retry only when repeating the operation is safe; never automatically retry state-changing operations without idempotency or another concrete safety mechanism.
Respect Retry-After or equivalent rate-limit guidance where appropriate; never retry indefinitely or aggressively.
Use a fallback only when its result is semantically acceptable; never hide correctness failures behind convenient default values.
Caller cancellation is not a transient failure: never retry it or convert it into repeated outbound attempts.
No caching without a clear measured or reasoned need; choose the implementation according to deployment, consistency and staleness requirements.
Cache keys uniquely represent the cached value including relevant user, tenant and context dimensions; no global keys for user- or tenant-specific data.
Every cache entry has a lifetime or another explicit invalidation strategy.
Invalidate/update cache entries only consistently with successful underlying mutations; the cache never becomes a second source of truth.
Anonymous access must be deliberate and visible; avoid redundant authorization attributes when a secure global or fallback policy already expresses the intent.
Do not implement custom token or password security, password hashing or reset-token cryptography when established ASP.NET Core authentication/Identity facilities cover the requirement.

Bearer/OIDC authentication validates what the actual issuer/provider requires (issuer, audience where applicable, signature/signing authority, lifetime); never disable validation merely to make a token work.
Authentication failures must not reveal secrets or account state unnecessarily; login avoids account-enumeration leaks where relevant.
Do not implement custom cryptography when a well-reviewed platform mechanism is appropriate, and do not treat ASP.NET Core Data Protection as universal database encryption.

CORS is the narrowest policy satisfying actual browser-client requirements (a public unauthenticated API may legitimately differ from a private browser application); never combine credentialed cross-origin requests with unrestricted origins.
Do not treat client-provided file metadata such as MIME type as authoritative when upload handling or security decisions depend on actual content.
NUnit is the .NET automated test framework; do not introduce a second test framework without a concrete reason.
exceptions: In an established project that deliberately uses another framework, follow that convention.

normative_action: Backend test projects must not have broader production-project references than their test scope requires; they follow the same inward dependency discipline as production projects.

Typical test references: <Name>.Domain.Tests (optional) -> Domain; <Name>.Application.Tests -> Application, Domain as needed; <Name>.IntegrationTests -> Api (other layers exercised through the host); <Name>.Infrastructure.Tests (optional) -> Infrastructure, narrower references as required.
modality: SHOULD (typical matrix; enforced by the architecture-style facet)

normative_action: Choose the narrowest test level that meaningfully verifies the behavior; integration tests when framework wiring, HTTP, persistence, serialization or authentication is the subject; no fixed unit/integration ratio.

Tests verify observable behavior, survive internal refactoring, do not test private calls or exact internal call sequences, and do not reproduce the implementation's algorithm; interaction verification only when the interaction is the specified behavior.
exceptions: interaction itself is the specified behavior

normative_action: WebApplicationFactory-based integration tests when routing, model binding, middleware, authentication/authorization, DI, repositories, the persistence technology or database persistence is what the test must prove.
Use the actual database provider when relational/provider behavior matters (Testcontainers optional); never claim provider fidelity from a test that runs against a different provider.
Tests are deterministic, independent of execution order and isolated from Production and Development data, uncontrolled external systems and shared mutable state.
Tests start from a known state and own their setup; never depend on development seed data or the order in which other tests run.
For small finite input/state spaces use explicit declarative cases instead of loops, branches, LINQ or generated case machinery; expected results are stated, not computed.
Descriptive test names communicating scenario/condition and expected behavior (e.g. MethodOrScenario_Condition_ExpectedBehavior) unless the project has an established convention.
Do not generate low-value tests merely to increase a coverage percentage.
Add a dependency only for a concrete current requirement; never install packages for hypothetical future use; an approved technology is not a reason to install it by default.
Every NuGet or npm addition or update runs the add-dependency workflow.
Never hardcode or commit real secrets, credentials, private keys, access/refresh tokens or production connection strings, including in example configuration files.

A local secret mechanism (e.g. dotnet user-secrets) for development and environment-specific secret injection or a managed secret store for deployed environments; do not assume a cloud provider the project has not chosen.

Data crossing the trusted boundary (HTTP requests, uploads, external responses, message payloads, user-provided identifiers and filters) is untrusted; validate it at the owning layer when assumptions matter.
Authorization is enforced on the server; frontend route guards, hidden/disabled UI actions and client checks are UX, not a security boundary.

Production traffic carrying credentials or sensitive data uses TLS; respect actual hosting topology (TLS may terminate at app, proxy, ingress, gateway or platform), so app-level HTTP-to-HTTPS redirection is not required where deployment already provides a secure transport boundary and redirection is not desired.
exceptions: secure transport boundary provided by deployment

normative_action: Never disable certificate validation to make an integration work.

Never log passwords, access/refresh tokens, private keys, authentication secrets or full payment credentials; avoid PII unless a concrete operational requirement exists and policy permits; lower log levels do not make sensitive data safe; prefer stable technical identifiers.
exceptions: concrete permitted operational need for PII

normative_action: Do not serialize arbitrary request bodies, domain objects or sensitive payloads into logs by default; log minimal useful non-sensitive context.
Security-sensitive authorization, permission and required-control checks fail safely; never silently convert a lookup or configuration failure into success.
A required security control that cannot be configured correctly fails visibly at startup/configuration time instead of falling back to an insecure mode.
Physical structure follows actual responsibilities; do not create speculative projects, infrastructure, empty directory trees or generic Common/Helpers/Utils buckets solely to look architectural.

npm is the frontend package manager unless deliberately changed; package.json and package-lock.json are committed and kept consistent; build/test tooling belongs in devDependencies unless there is a concrete reason.
exceptions: deliberate package-manager change; concrete reason for runtime placement

normative_action: Modern standalone Angular APIs for new code (no new NgModules for ordinary feature development), with code organized primarily by feature.
Signals for naturally synchronous local UI state; RxJS when async streams, HTTP composition, cancellation or event pipelines are clearer; avoid mechanical conversions.
Functional HTTP interceptors for new code; interceptors stay cross-cutting and never contain feature business logic.

Use reactive forms for non-trivial forms when explicit state, validation and testability are useful; frontend validation is UX and never replaces backend validation or data-integrity/security enforcement.
Avoid manual nested RxJS subscriptions; prefer composition operators when stream composition expresses the behavior clearly.
A manual RxJS subscription from Angular framework-managed code is tied to the component/service lifecycle using current Angular facilities (e.g. takeUntilDestroyed).

Frontend structure stays feature-oriented: no application-wide technical buckets (global components/, services/, models/) or empty architecture folders; feature-specific code stays inside its feature; core/shared stay small.
Pages and components stay focused on presentation and UI orchestration; do not move trivial presentation logic into services merely to make components smaller.
Route-level lazy loading for meaningful features; do not lazy-load every tiny component.
Simple local, component or feature-service state before introducing a state-management library.

Backend communication lives in explicit feature data-access services or another explicit HTTP boundary; never scatter HTTP calls through presentation components and never import backend Domain types into the frontend (use frontend API models matching the published HTTP contract).
Frontend code follows the documented API error contract: centralize reusable ProblemDetails parsing when practical and never infer business behavior from arbitrary human-readable exception messages.
When browser cookies automatically carry authentication credentials, CSRF protection is part of the design; never assume the SPA framework removes that risk.
exceptions: Bearer tokens attached explicitly via the Authorization header have different CSRF characteristics.

normative_action: Never claim one browser token-storage mechanism is universally secure; choose token storage by the application's threat model and never log tokens.

Adding or removing a non-test backend project (a .csproj appearing or disappearing relative to the baseline) without an accepted decision naming the project in the decision register is reported as an error (Reserved, recorded approval required).
exceptions: Test projects (Tests/IntegrationTests naming) are exempt; changes already in HEAD are not flagged.

normative_action: When CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md changes, the agent is told to run the custom-settings workflow to synchronize affected surfaces.
trigger_scope: Edits/commands changing CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md (pending change vs HEAD)

normative_action: When SPECIFICATION.md changes, the agent is told to check consistency with CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md and synchronize affected code, tests and docs (development-workflow).
Deleting a Directory.Packages.props central package management file is reported as an error.

When instruction files change (CLAUDE.md, docs/architecture/decision-register.md, .claude/** except settings.local.json), the instruction-structure checker runs and its errors are fed back to the agent for correction through the template-maintenance workflow.
trigger_scope: Edit/Write/MultiEdit or shell commands touching instruction files
exceptions: Warnings are not fed back; only checker errors.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Structural self-validation of the instruction system; no oracle policy constrains instruction-file structure.

normative_action: Path-scoped standards live directly in .claude/rules/<scope>/ using only the scope directories common, backend, backend-tests, frontend, delivery (no deeper hierarchy); the header Scope equals the directory; every rule declares frontmatter paths: that include its scope's canonical glob (common **/*, backend backend/**/*, backend-tests backend/**/*Tests/**/*, frontend frontend/**/*).
exceptions: Delivery rules declare their own CI/container globs (no canonical glob).
why_extra_or_uncertain: Loading/organization rule of the K1 instruction system; no V2 policy regulates rule-file layout or globs.

normative_action: CLAUDE.md must @-import the decision register; only OP/DEC artifacts may be @-imported into the always-loaded surface, every import must resolve, and no Markdown file other than CLAUDE.md may contain @ imports.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Always-loaded-surface composition rule of the template; not a V2 policy.

normative_action: Skill inventory and structure: every skill directory has a SKILL.md whose frontmatter name equals the directory name and which has a description (warning above 450 characters: keep concise and trigger-first); required workflows (project-structure, verify, code-review, build-fix, custom-settings, git-workflow, security-scan, add-dependency, architecture-decision, template-maintenance) exist as Kind WF; required knowledge skills (http-api, aspnet-error-handling, logging, httpclient-factory, configuration, dependency-injection, caching, swagger, api-versioning, health-check, docker, ci-cd, modern-csharp, authentication) exist as Kind KNW; standalone serilog or resilience skills are forbidden (use a private reference of the owning knowledge skill).
modality: MUST (structure checker error; description length warning)
why_extra_or_uncertain: Template inventory constraint; the oracle prescribes no skill inventory, naming or packaging.

normative_action: Instruction references must resolve: no references to unknown skills, no unresolved or ambiguous file references; skill-private references/ files are used only by their owning skill; conformance dependencies must not form cycles.
exceptions: References to absent facet roles of a slot selected none are dormant, not errors.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Referential-integrity rule of the instruction system; not a V2 policy.

normative_action: Hook configuration: settings.json registers only and all of PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure and Stop; each hook uses exec form (command node with args [${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/dispatch.cjs, <event>]) without shell-variable expansion in command, a timeout of 1-600 seconds, and matchers covering Bash|PowerShell (PreToolUse, PostToolUseFailure) and Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash|PowerShell (PostToolUse); only the PreToolUse dependency/reference guard fails closed (onFailure block) and advisory hooks must not block on failure; the dispatcher must have a handler for each event.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Enforcement-configuration invariants of the template; no oracle policy requires hooks or their configuration.

normative_action: Normative text in OP, DEC and STD artifacts avoids the ambiguous word 'normally' and uses must/default/prefer vocabulary instead.
trigger_scope: Authoring always-loaded and path-scoped normative text
exceptions: Warning only; not applied to KNW/WF artifacts.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Authoring-vocabulary rule of the template; the oracle itself uses 'normally' in several policies and imposes no vocabulary rule.

normative_action: The always-loaded surface (CLAUDE.md, its imports, names/descriptions of model-invocable skills and agent descriptions) stays near a 5k-token target; above about 6000 estimated tokens a warning is raised.
exceptions: Warning only; skills with disable-model-invocation are not counted.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Context-budget rule of the template design; not a V2 policy.

normative_action: The NuGet packages Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly and Polly.Extensions.Http are denied as deprecated resilience integration packages (error in project files and in Directory.Packages.props).
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-020 treats direct Polly integration as an explicit exception rather than a prohibition, and DEP-004 requires checking deprecation before installation but sets no fixed deny list; the candidate makes these two packages hard errors regardless of any explicit decision.

normative_action: Central PackageVersion entries need an exact version: a missing, floating (*) or range version is an error; a prerelease version is warned as allowed only when explicitly requested.

package.json dependency specs must not float: empty, *, x, latest or next are errors in dependencies, devDependencies, peerDependencies and optionalDependencies; prerelease specs (alpha, beta, rc, next, canary, dev, preview) are warned as allowed only when explicitly requested.
exceptions: Caret/tilde ranges are not flagged by this post-check (only the pre-execution install gate RULE-K1-0004 demands exact versions).

normative_action: Direct Polly or Polly.Core package usage is flagged as a documented exception (warning) to the Microsoft resilience default.
A top-level tests/ directory is flagged: backend tests live beside production projects.
Directory.Packages.props must enable ManagePackageVersionsCentrally; a project PackageReference declaring a Version is an error and a VersionOverride is warned to record its reason.

Build/test tooling (typescript, vitest, eslint, prettier, jest, @playwright/test, karma, jasmine-core, @types/*) placed in runtime dependencies is warned, and a frontend package.json without an adjacent package-lock.json is warned.

A backend production project may reference only inward roles (Domain: none; Application: Domain; Infrastructure: Application, Domain; Api: Application, Infrastructure, Domain); any other production reference and any production -> test-project reference is an error.
exceptions: Projects outside backend/ are not checked.

normative_action: Test-project references: the typical target (Domain.Tests -> Domain; Application.Tests -> Application, Domain; Infrastructure.Tests -> Infrastructure; Api.Tests and IntegrationTests -> Api) passes; broader but justifiable references (Infrastructure.Tests -> Application/Domain; Api.Tests/IntegrationTests -> Application/Infrastructure/Domain) are warned to keep only if required; other production references are errors; test -> test references are warned.
exceptions: Generic *.Tests projects without a layer target are not checked.

normative_action: Domain and Application projects must not use the Web SDK (Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web), reference the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework, or reference Microsoft.AspNetCore.* packages.
@ngrx/*, axios, lodash/lodash-es, bootstrap, @ng-bootstrap/*, ngx-bootstrap and tailwindcss in a frontend package.json are warned as not added by default; the concrete need must be confirmed.
modality: MUST NOT by default (frontend facet check: warning)

normative_action: Angular build tooling (@angular/cli, @angular/build, @angular-devkit/*, @angular/compiler-cli) in runtime dependencies is warned (belongs in devDependencies).
Domain and Application projects must not reference EF Core packages (Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore and Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.*).

Test projects referencing xUnit (incl. xunit.v3/xunit.core), MSTest (incl. TestFramework/TestAdapter) or TUnit packages, in addition to or instead of NUnit, and central versions for those frameworks, are warned: introducing another test framework needs a concrete reason.
exceptions: Warning only; concrete reason permits it.

normative_action: Before adding a dependency, the choice must match the decision register's approved stack; anything else goes through architecture-decision first.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Open question: if 'anything else' covers any package not named in the register (e.g. a small utility library for a concern with no approved technology), the clause makes every non-stack dependency a Reserved decision, which is stricter than DEP-001/DEP-002 (need-based additions are allowed; only silent replacement of an approved technology needs approval). If it only means alternatives to an approved technology, it restates DEP-002. The text does not settle which reading applies.

normative_action: A dependency choice that departs from the decision register's approved stack goes through architecture-decision before installation (no silent alternative).

API versioning uses the Controller integration of Asp.Versioning (Asp.Versioning.Mvc, plus Asp.Versioning.Mvc.ApiExplorer for documentation), added only after the project has adopted API versioning, never before.
When resilience is required use Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience for HttpClient and Microsoft.Extensions.Resilience for general pipelines; direct Polly usage is an explicit, documented exception.
Mapster (with Mapster.DependencyInjection) is never referenced from Domain.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-011 approves Mapster when mapping volume warrants it and ARC-002 keeps Domain free of EF Core, ASP.NET Core, HTTP, persistence and external-service concerns; no oracle policy forbids a mapping library in Domain.

normative_action: Mapster with Mapster.DependencyInjection is added once mapping volume warrants it; Testcontainers, Playwright and similar conditional packages are added per the decision register (only when the capability is adopted).

For every NuGet or npm addition or update, determine the latest stable version compatible with target framework/runtime and peers, verify it from the registry rather than memory, and never select preview/alpha/beta/RC/dev/nightly/prerelease or floating versions unless the user explicitly requested them ('latest' means latest stable compatible).

Before installation, confirm the selected package/version is not deprecated, check known vulnerability information (dotnet package list --vulnerable --include-transitive, npm audit, advisories) with context and without upgrading or replacing unrelated packages because of a finding, and verify the exact version's license from official registry metadata (permissive MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD may be accepted; free download does not imply an acceptable license).

Do not automatically install paid/commercial or materially restrictive/unclear-license dependencies (strong copyleft, dual licensing that may require a commercial license, source-available/custom, unclear or missing license); explain the concern and present choices without silently substituting an alternative; say so when no reasonable free alternative exists; draw no legal conclusions beyond the published license.

NuGet installs add/update the PackageVersion in Directory.Packages.props and reference the package without a version only from the narrowest project that needs it (dotnet add <project> package <id> --version <version>).
npm installs use npm install <name>@<version> (--save-dev for build/test tooling) and keep package-lock.json consistent and committed.
Resolve peer-dependency conflicts at their cause; never use npm --force or --legacy-peer-deps merely to bypass incompatible peer dependencies.
Remove dependencies that are no longer used when doing so is part of the current change and safe to verify; do not leave dead package references behind.
trigger_scope: Changes that make a dependency unused
exceptions: Not during unrelated cleanup of a narrowly scoped task.
why_extra_or_uncertain: No oracle policy requires removing packages made unused by a change (RUN-010 covers only unused usings in changed C# files); the candidate adds a cleanup obligation.

normative_action: Do not perform unrelated dependency cleanup during a narrowly scoped task.
After a dependency change, build and run affected tests (verify) and report the package, version, license, due-diligence results and any approval obtained or pending.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 requires reporting what verification actually ran; no oracle policy requires reporting package, version, license and due-diligence outcomes for each dependency change.

normative_action: After a dependency change, build and run the affected tests through verify.
Frontend tests use the workspace's configured runner (Vitest for new projects); Playwright E2E only when adopted.

Frontend tests target meaningful component behavior, validation, data-access request mapping, important route/auth behavior and complex reactive state; do not test framework internals or duplicate the same behavior at every level; E2E covers a small number of important user workflows unless broader coverage is required.

Do not prematurely optimize the frontend: lazy loading and sensible rendering/data access first; memoization, virtual scrolling, custom change detection and similar optimizations only after identifying a real need.

When the project has chosen Angular Material, use its components consistently for common UI primitives where they satisfy the requirement; do not add it to projects that have not chosen it; do not wrap every Material component in a custom abstraction without a concrete reason.

When OpenAPI client generation is adopted, keep generated code separate from handwritten feature logic, regenerate it when the API contract changes, and do not patch generated files unless the generation workflow requires it.
Do not duplicate complex Domain rules in TypeScript unless the UI genuinely needs an equivalent user-facing rule.
exceptions: UI needs an equivalent user-facing rule.

normative_action: Deprecation is a migration process: mark the version deprecated (ApiVersion Deprecated = true with ReportApiVersions) and document the replacement, migration period and removal timing (procedure: development-workflow).

Classify a decision with the Reserved list and five-question test from CLAUDE.md: Delegated proceeds without the decision workflow; Decided follows the existing record, and reopening a Decided decision is itself Reserved.

For a Reserved choice present a Decision Request (title, context, 2-3 realistic options with trade-offs/reversibility/cost, recommendation citing the governing policy, Blocked work, Proceeding-with compliant work) and stop the affected work until the user answers; compliant non-Reserved work may continue.
exceptions: Compliant non-Reserved work may proceed meanwhile.

normative_action: Headless or autonomous runs follow CLAUDE.md decision control and must not silently take Reserved decisions; the Decision Request's Proceeding-with field names the compliant path actually taken.

After approval, record the accepted decision as a row of the decision register's Accepted decisions table (date, decision, scope, record link) and update the affected register section (stack, conditional technology, project default or capability selection).
For a consequential or non-obvious accepted decision, add a docs/decisions/NNNN-short-title.md record (context, decision, alternatives considered, consequences, date, approver).
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-017 requires approval of Reserved changes and GOV-007 synchronization of approved product rules, but no oracle policy requires a separate architecture decision record with fixed content.

normative_action: The architecture-decision workflow reports the decision, its class, the approval source, register/record updates and any request still unresolved.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Reporting duty specific to the decision workflow; WF-009 covers verification reporting only.

normative_action: Register FluentValidation validators with FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions and do not add deprecated/legacy ASP.NET automatic-validation integration packages.
exceptions: Follow the project's established invocation pattern instead of adding a competing one.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-010 makes FluentValidation the standard library but prescribes no registration package; no oracle policy forbids the ASP.NET automatic-validation integration packages outright (DEP-004 only requires a deprecation check).

normative_action: Never cache tracked persistence entities across Unit of Work boundaries.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-021 governs invalidation consistency and ARC-017 the shared scoped context, but no oracle policy forbids caching tracked entities across Unit of Work scopes.

normative_action: Catch exceptions only to recover, translate into a meaningful abstraction-level outcome, perform necessary cleanup, add context while preserving the original, apply a defined fallback or infrastructure retry; otherwise let them propagate; never swallow external-service failures or catch Exception merely to continue.

A Result<T> pattern is optional: consider it when an operation has several expected failure modes and it will be used consistently; avoid it where null/bool/simple typed responses suffice; project-wide adoption is a Reserved decision (CLAUDE.md decision control).

Choose the authentication scheme by the actual application (Bearer/OIDC for SPA->API, cookies for server-rendered apps, Identity when the app owns local users, external OIDC/OAuth when identity is delegated); a business entity named User or profile management does not justify Identity, and do not issue custom JWTs when an existing identity provider owns token issuance.
A new authentication/authorization architecture is a Reserved decision.
Build-fix restores the affected scope to green without hiding failures, weakening behavior or introducing unrelated changes.

Reproduce and diagnose the actual failure (narrowest reproducing command, complete output, errors grouped by root cause) before editing; never guess at a fix first; fix root causes before downstream symptoms.

Repair in small bounded iterations: smallest correct change, rerun the same narrowest failing check and compare failure sets, expand verification only after the focused failure is resolved; stop and reassess when progress stalls (same root failure survives different fixes, growing unrelated failures, incompatible toolchain, unavailable infrastructure) and never repeat variants of the same failed guess.

Do not weaken, delete, skip or suppress relevant tests, compiler, TypeScript, lint or analyzer failures merely to pass; understand a diagnostic before changing how it is reported; never turn a strong assertion into a weak one or delete/skip a failing test because fixing it is inconvenient.
Preserve architecture and project conventions while fixing; a green build obtained by violating them is not a successful repair.

Determine the affected scope and do not run unrelated build systems merely because they exist (backend-only failure: the affected .NET project; frontend failure: the workspace; API contract consumed by the frontend: both; documentation-only: no application builds without a reason).
For the frontend, inspect package.json and use scripts that actually exist; never invent script names or assume a test runner.
exceptions: Applies the CI-scoped WF-018 rule to local repair as well.

normative_action: Do not use invalid repair shortcuts: invalid project references (e.g. Application -> Infrastructure), leaking persistence types into Application, business logic in controllers, frontend-only authorization, scattering HTTP calls into components; frontend: converting to any to silence the compiler, disabling strict mode, suppressing template diagnostics without understanding, replacing framework APIs speculatively, adding another state-management or HTTP library to bypass a local issue.

For full-stack/contract failures determine the authoritative contract; never patch both sides independently into inconsistent shapes; with OpenAPI generation verify the backend contract, regenerate the client through the normal workflow, review generated changes, then fix handwritten frontend code.
If expected behavior intentionally changed, update the test to express the new contract and confirm the change was actually requested.
Never replace a package or add another merely to get a green build; never duplicate conflicting versions in .csproj files (Central Package Management); never delete package-lock.json reflexively.

For upgrade fallout update obsolete APIs deliberately from verified documentation (never fabricate replacement APIs from memory) without unrelated upgrades; never change the declared SDK, Node, framework or language version merely because the local machine differs, and report an unavailable toolchain as a limitation instead of editing source to compensate.

When generated output is wrong or its source contract/configuration changed, identify the generator and input, fix the authoritative source and regenerate (OpenAPI clients, source generators, persistence migrations, frontend build output); do not manually patch disposable generated output unless the repository or generation workflow treats it as maintained source.

If a fix introduces new failures, determine whether they are a legitimate dependency of the change or revert/correct the fix; never leave the repository knowingly worse than where the repair started; do not clean up unrelated pre-existing failures unless they block verification or the user asks.
A behavioral test or probe used to establish correct behavior during diagnosis is preserved in maintained tests (verify step 4) before temporary diagnostics are removed.

A repair is complete when the affected scope is green (relevant builds and affected tests pass, cross-stack contracts consistent, no known new regression, no accidental workaround in the diff), without requiring unrelated builds; then run verify for the final completion pass when appropriate.

Report repairs with backend build, frontend build and tests as PASS / NOT RUN / NOT APPLICABLE plus root cause, changes and remaining issues; never claim the problem is fixed while a known relevant failure remains.
Adding a distributed cache (multi-instance shared cache, HybridCache L2, Redis) is a Reserved infrastructure decision, added only when deployment requirements justify it.

With caching, Application Services keep their normal repository/Unit of Work workflow and coordinate required invalidation through an abstraction rather than bypassing repositories or IUnitOfWork; decide explicitly whether a cache failure falls back to the source, fails the request or returns stale data.
Add frontend unit-test and lint CI steps only when the workspace's package.json defines those scripts.

Provide CI integration-test services (database, cache, broker) only when tests require them, isolated from Development and Production data; do not hardcode a database provider into a generic pipeline.
Build and publish container images in CI only when container deployment is part of the project; do not assume container deployment.
Generate database migration scripts/artifacts in CI and execute them at a controlled deployment step with approved credentials, failing visibly on error.

The review is independent and read-only: it reports findings and does not edit files or rewrite working code unless asked; this workflow is the canonical review procedure; verify, not code review, performs the final build/test/diff verification.

Prioritize findings: correctness; security and authorization; data integrity and persistence; architectural boundary violations; concurrency and integration; missing meaningful tests; maintainability; credible performance; never elevate style above behavioral defects and do not report formatting owned by tooling.

Establish the review scope and read enough surrounding code (callers, contracts, dependencies) and the governing standards and relevant knowledge to understand changed behavior; never review isolated lines; check architecture against the loaded owners rather than a private checklist.
Do not introduce or enforce patterns the repository has not adopted (differing from an unadopted pattern is not a finding); report only correctness failures with a plausible execution path.

Review specification conformance in both directions: required behavior is not missing or weakened and no unapproved behavior is introduced (new lengths/limits, reserved names/values, observable string-comparison semantics incl. database configuration or framework defaults, new required fields, extra workflow restrictions, additional user-visible validation); approved synchronized details are not drift; internal implementation details are not product behavior.
trigger_scope: Code review with non-empty SPECIFICATION.md / CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md

normative_action: Architecture review checks role/dependency rules, repository/persistence boundary, proportionality (consequential patterns only with approved need) and, when the persistence model changed, that persistence-change steps including the development seeder were followed; frontend code is checked against frontend rules without mechanically applying backend project-boundary rules.

Review data and security aspects (commit behavior, destructive changes, raw SQL parameterization, authorization, trust boundaries, secrets, sensitive logging, concurrency, migrations, cache consistency); run the full security-scan only when an audit was requested, the change is materially security-sensitive, or a concrete finding justifies it.
Review external calls for cancellation, timeouts, idempotency, retry safety, failure translation and lifetime; never demand retries for operations that are not safe to retry.

Check that changed behavior has useful maintained coverage; for bug fixes look for a regression test when recurrence is plausible; behavioral probes must be preserved as maintained tests; do not request duplicate tests when equivalent coverage exists.
Report performance only for credible reasons (N+1, unbounded materialization, blocking async I/O, repeated expensive remote calls, demonstrated hot paths); do not recommend speculative optimizations.
Review must not require an MCP server or specific analyzer; tool output is evidence, not authority — read the code before turning a warning into a finding.
trigger_scope: Code review (applies the security-review tool-independence rule to review)

normative_action: Report findings ordered by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low) with location, what is wrong, why it matters and the smallest reasonable fix.
Never invent findings to populate a category; when there are no meaningful findings say so and name important areas that could not be verified; no filler praise.
Numeric values in configuration examples are illustrative, not approved defaults; choose retry counts, timeouts and limits from the actual integration and deployment requirements.
A CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md value must be approved before synchronization; new values are proposed with a reason and approved first.
A conflict between a setting and SPECIFICATION.md stops the workflow until the user decides which source to correct.
Only values that belong in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md per CLAUDE.md product-source rules are recorded there, not merely framework defaults the project has not intentionally overridden.

Record the setting in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md with a stable descriptive name, its value and its purpose; avoid duplicating the same literal across many layers when a single source in code or configuration is appropriate.

When a value is added, changed or removed, search for the old value, the setting name, validators/DTO constraints, Domain/Application checks, persistence mapping constraints, frontend validation and UI hints, tests and test data, docs/examples and mirrored configuration; distinguish coincidental numbers and update every affected implementation, validation, configuration, test, documentation and mirrored frontend/backend surface.
exceptions: Unrelated numeric coincidences are left alone.

normative_action: When a setting affects schema constraints, indexes, column lengths or other persistence metadata, update the persistence mapping, create the appropriate migration per the migration workflow, verify Development seeding remains valid, add/update provider-sensitive tests when provider behavior matters, and do not casually alter existing migrations (persistence-change).
When both sides expose the same constraint, backend validation stays authoritative; frontend validation and messages are kept synchronized for UX and never relied on for security or data integrity.
trigger_scope: Settings mirrored in frontend and backend

normative_action: Before completion search for stale references to the old value, build affected projects, run relevant tests, verify persistence changes when applicable, recheck SPECIFICATION.md for conflicts and run verify; changing one literal alone does not establish synchronization.
The custom-settings report lists the setting, old -> new value, every updated surface, any migration created and the verify result.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Reporting duty specific to the workflow; WF-009 requires reporting verification state only, not a per-setting surface inventory.

normative_action: Containers are optional infrastructure: do not introduce Docker merely because the application can be containerized; build images and deployable artifacts only when the project deploys them.

Before writing a pipeline or container file inspect the repository (backend, frontend, test projects, Dockerfiles, provider-specific tests, generated clients, deployment artifacts); do not assume a database provider, cache, container or frontend tooling exists, and add stages for the actual project, not generic boilerplate.

CI definitions live in source control, reproduce the repository's supported build and test commands, and never hide build or test failures (no suppressed tests, ignored exit codes or continue-on-error for required checks).

Frontend CI uses scripts that actually exist in the workspace's package.json and npm ci when a maintained lockfile supports it; never invent npm scripts and never reflexively replace a lockfile-based install with npm install.

Enforced formatting/analyzer gates only when the project has adopted them; dependency vulnerability inspection per the project's security policy; no automatic package upgrades unless the project adopted automated updates.

Production database migrations must not run automatically from normal application startup by default: a production migration is an explicit deployment step at a controlled point with the project's approved credentials that fails visibly on error; Development seeding never runs in Production (also unchanged by container deployment).

Before considering a pipeline complete verify that it restores from a clean environment, builds backend and (when present) frontend, runs the configured tests, does not depend on developer-machine state, does not expose secrets and produces expected artifacts; report each item as PASS / NOT RUN / NOT APPLICABLE.

Prefer explicit DI registration in small and medium applications; add assembly scanning, keyed services, factories or decorators (and Scrutor) only when they solve an actual composition problem — e.g. no Scrutor for a single decoration, scanning only for genuine registration boilerplate and over the assembly that owns the services.
Before planning or implementing a new application or substantial feature read SPECIFICATION.md (and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md when tunable values are involved).

Before any non-trivial change inspect the relevant existing code, read the applicable standards for the touched areas, load the relevant knowledge skills, and route specialized work to its workflow (persistence-change, custom-settings, project-structure, delivery-change).
For a questionable request apply the challenge obligation from CLAUDE.md before implementing.
Keep the change inside the requested scope.
For a meaningful bug whose recurrence is plausible add a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after it, unless equivalent coverage already exists or recurrence is unrealistic.

A performance-motivated change identifies the actual bottleneck or cost, preserves observable behavior, uses the simplest effective optimization, adds or maintains tests for affected behavior, and benchmarks or profiles non-obvious or complex optimizations.

When deprecating an externally consumed API version mark the deprecation in versioning metadata, document the replacement, communicate a realistic migration period and removal timeline, and keep the old version working for the promised support period; never remove it without considering its published support contract.

When a new behavioral rule is approved update the durable source of truth in the same change, including SPECIFICATION.md when appropriate; approved tunable values follow custom-settings and accepted engineering decisions follow architecture-decision.
For substantial feature work or a newly implemented application run code-review (or the code-reviewer agent) before final verification and fix confirmed findings.
Before declaring implementation complete run verify at the depth the change's scope and risk require.
The development-workflow final report summarizes what changed and why, the verify report, approvals obtained and every unresolved Decision Request.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 requires reporting actual verification state; the duty to report the change rationale, approvals and every unresolved Decision Request is an additional reporting obligation.

normative_action: For container work build the image and verify application startup, required port/configuration, non-root behavior when relevant, health-probe integration and the absence of accidental secrets/files; run meaningful tests outside or as part of the pipeline.

Do not build test infrastructure without a concrete testing need (no enterprise-sized harness for a small project, no generic test-data framework for a few simple objects, no snapshot library by default).

Convert temporary behavioral checks (ad-hoc HTTP/curl/PowerShell requests, temporary scripts or test methods, manual database checks, regression probes) into maintained tests, verify that an existing test really exercises the behavior instead of adding a duplicate, and review probes before promoting them.
Use the persistence provider the project actually selected; never add a provider because an example shows it.

Infrastructure pipeline hooks — EF Core interceptors and HTTP DelegatingHandlers — are used only for infrastructure-level cross-cutting behavior with a clear benefit (auditing, auth headers, correlation, request signing); never hide business behavior or business decisions in them.

SQL Server string comparison follows column/database collation (default case-insensitive); choosing case sensitivity or a collation is a product decision when observable, and an approved choice is made explicit with UseCollation(...) or a column-level collation.
Never fire-and-forget EF Core asynchronous operations; a DbContext is not thread-safe.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-002 forbids blocking async I/O and ARC-022 governs DI lifetimes; no oracle policy forbids un-awaited (fire-and-forget) database operations or concurrent DbContext use.

normative_action: Do not wrap normal database operations in a generic application-level retry pipeline or apply an HTTP retry policy to them; database transient faults use the persistence provider's execution strategy (EnableRetryOnFailure), with explicit transactions wrapped in the execution strategy.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-016 limits retries to safe operations and DEP-020 sets the default resilience packages, but no oracle policy prescribes provider-level execution strategies or forbids application-level retry pipelines for database calls (the oracle treats database-retry examples as technique, EXC-007).

normative_action: Never discard, overwrite, reset, clean, stash away or otherwise destroy user work to make a Git operation easier.

Before any repository-changing operation inspect the relevant state (git status, git diff, git diff --cached) and use the minimum operation required; never silently clean unrelated working-tree changes.

Treat git reset --hard, git clean, git push --force/--force-with-lease, branch deletion and rebasing shared history as high-risk: perform them only when explicitly requested (or clearly required by an approved workflow) and only after inspecting what will be lost or rewritten.
exceptions: 'clearly required by an approved workflow' (see UNCERTAIN UNCERTAIN-K1-0003)

normative_action: High-risk Git operations may be performed when 'clearly required by an approved workflow', not only when explicitly requested.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Open question: GOV-015 permits repository-changing Git operations only when explicitly requested; whether 'clearly required by an approved workflow' merely refers to a workflow the user explicitly requested (entailed) or lets a workflow trigger destructive operations without a specific request (a relaxation) is not determinable from the text.

normative_action: Before committing inspect the staged diff: it contains only the intended logical change; never stage or clean unrelated files merely because they are modified; prefer one logical change per commit with implementation and its tests together, no artificial tiny commits and no combined unrelated fixes/refactors.

Follow the repository's branch-naming convention (defaults feature/, fix/, refactor/, test/, docs/, chore/), do not rename an existing user branch to satisfy a convention, never check one branch out in multiple normal worktrees, keep each worktree focused, and never remove a worktree containing uncommitted user work (verify preservation first).

Before pushing confirm the intended branch and understood working/staged state, ensure relevant verification completed and avoid pushing unrelated local commits; never force-push a shared branch unless the user explicitly requests history rewriting and understands the consequences.
Treat main, master and other protected/shared branches as non-rewritable.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-015 allows force-push and other history-changing operations when explicitly requested; declaring main/master non-rewritable is stricter (read literally, even an explicit request does not unlock rewriting them).

normative_action: For merge/rebase follow the repository/team convention or the user's explicit request, inspect local uncommitted work first and never automatically stash, reset or discard it; resolve conflicts from the intended combined behavior rather than mechanically choosing ours/theirs, and run relevant verification afterwards.
Run verify before preparing a PR; a PR has a focused purpose without accidental unrelated changes; never claim checks that were not run.
A pull request description explains what changed, why, how it was verified and compatibility/migration notes.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 covers truthful verification reporting; no oracle policy fixes PR description content.

normative_action: Resilience mechanisms are added only when failure and operation semantics justify them (standard handler not mandatory for every client; no stacked handlers with overlapping strategies); configure them through the Microsoft.Extensions resilience APIs.
Apply per-request values such as dynamic access tokens to the specific request or through a handler; never mutate a shared HttpClient's DefaultRequestHeaders concurrently.
exceptions: Stable headers (media types) may be configured on the client.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-005 governs HttpClient lifetime only; no oracle policy forbids mutating shared default headers.

normative_action: Confirm the configured language version supports a feature before using it; never silently change LangVersion or the target framework to use newer syntax (a platform change is Reserved).
