When explicitly asked to modernize: preserve behavior, keep the change focused, prefer readability improvements, build and test afterwards, and do not mix architecture refactoring into syntax modernization.

Persistence setup installs Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer in Infrastructure through add-dependency, Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design only where design-time tooling needs it (startup project), and dotnet-ef as a local tool when the CLI is used.
Regenerate or edit an uncommitted migration only when that matches the project's migration workflow; never casually alter migrations that are already applied or shared.

Review the generated migration as source code before it is committed, paying particular attention to destructive schema changes, unexpected column recreation, data migrations, indexes, foreign keys and delete behavior.

Whenever a Domain or persistence change affects seeded entities (new required or removed/renamed properties, changed relationships, new required related entities, changed enum/status values, new meaningful states, changed invariants) update the maintained development seeder in the same change so that recreating an empty Development database yields valid representative data; existing seeded rows are not patched automatically.
Add or update persistence/integration tests when provider behavior, mappings, constraints or non-trivial queries changed.
why_extra_or_uncertain: PST-009 requires updating provider-sensitive tests only for schema-affecting CUSTOM_SETTINGS changes and TST-007 governs provider fidelity, not when tests must be added; no oracle policy obliges new or updated tests for every mapping/constraint/query change.

normative_action: After persistence changes build, run affected tests, start the API against a freshly recreated Development database when seeding or the schema changed, run check-cochange, then continue with verify.
The persistence-change report lists model changes, migration name and review notes (destructive operations called out), seeder updates and verification results.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 requires truthful verification reporting; reporting migration review notes and seeder updates is an extra workflow report duty.

normative_action: Controllers are the HTTP endpoint mechanism; create Minimal API endpoint groups only when explicitly requested.

Backend test projects live beside production projects under backend/ (no top-level tests directory); create only useful ones — Domain.Tests and Infrastructure.Tests only for non-trivial behavior; a simple Domain of entities and enums needs no dedicated test project.

Create the frontend with the latest stable Angular release supported by the selected Node.js environment through the current Angular CLI, letting the CLI select compatible TypeScript/RxJS versions (no independent TypeScript upgrade beyond Angular's supported range); accept zoneless mode when supported; Vitest is the baseline test runner for new projects; add Angular Material/CDK matching the workspace version through add-dependency checks.
Frontend scaffolding ends with 'Verify with the workspace's declared scripts ... and commit package-lock.json'.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Open question: if 'commit package-lock.json' instructs the agent to run git commit during scaffolding, it conflicts with GOV-015 (repository-changing Git operations only on explicit request); if it only means the lockfile must be tracked in version control (as in rules/frontend/dependencies.md), it restates DEP-007. The imperative step wording does not settle which.

normative_action: Frontend unit/component tests stay inside the frontend workspace (normally colocated), E2E tests (Playwright, only when E2E coverage is required) live inside the workspace (e.g. frontend/ProjectName.Web/e2e/), and frontend tests are never placed under backend/.

The default physical repository layout (backend/, frontend/<Name>.Web/, docs/, shared root files) is a target structure: create optional directories or projects (including docs/ subdirectories) only when needed.
The solution file uses the .slnx format.
exceptions: Legacy .sln only when an external tool or requirement needs it (register).

normative_action: Directory.Build.props holds genuinely shared settings (TargetFramework, Nullable, ImplicitUsings, analysis/compiler settings), never project-specific settings.

The repository includes a global.json pinning the intended supported SDK line: the current stable SDK for the target .NET release (no RC/preview unless explicitly requested), with servicing allowed by the chosen rollForward policy.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-008 fixes the platform (.NET 10 LTS, no preview without approval) but no oracle policy requires an SDK-pinning global.json file.

normative_action: Docker files, deployment manifests, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, messaging infrastructure and additional services are introduced only for a concrete requirement; optional infrastructure is not scaffolded because it may be useful later.

Scaffolding is verified by restoring, building the .NET solution and the frontend when present, running relevant tests, inspecting project references (check-manifests), inspecting the final tree and confirming the Development configuration, then running verify; never report successful scaffolding when the result does not build; complete only when structure matches scope, references respect the architecture, approved technology is used and nothing unnecessary or unrelated was created.

Before adding a project later determine whether a new assembly is justified and identify its responsibility; a new production project or layer is Reserved (architecture-decision); never split code into additional projects merely to look sophisticated.

Reorganize an existing solution only for a concrete structural problem: inspect tree and references, preserve behavior, move code in small reviewable steps, update namespaces/references consistently, avoid unrelated feature work, verify; do not force an established project to match the template without concrete value.

Do not introduce by default MediatR, CQRS handler trees, Vertical Slice Architecture, Domain Events, Specifications, SharedKernel, BuildingBlocks, EventBus, messaging, microservices, Kubernetes, cloud-specific projects or state-management frameworks; each requires an approved need.
Normative vocabulary: must / must not — a violation is a defect; Default — deviation needs a concrete reason and must be reported; Prefer / avoid — guidance; Requires approval — a Reserved decision.
trigger_scope: All normative text and all deviations from Default rules
why_extra_or_uncertain: The oracle grades policies (MUST, DEFAULT, REQUIRES_APPROVAL) but defines no duty to report every deviation from a Default; the reporting duty and the 'defect' classification change how all Default rules bind.

normative_action: Unclear decisions are Reserved if any answer is yes: (1) adds, removes or replaces a dependency, framework or infrastructure capability; (2) changes a project/layer/reference boundary; (3) establishes a convention other code is expected to follow; (4) changes observable behavior or a public contract; (5) would be expensive to reverse after other code depends on it.
exceptions: Routine local decisions already constrained by the specification, register, existing code or standards are not escalated.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-017 requires a Decided/Delegated/Reserved classification and ARC-020 lists consequential choices, but neither defines this five-question test; question 1 alone makes any dependency addition/removal or replacement in an unclear case approval-gated, which DEP-001..DEP-005 do not.

normative_action: Adopting a new architectural style or pattern (CQRS, a mediator, Vertical Slice Architecture, event sourcing, microservices, a Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical patterns, a project-wide Result model) is Reserved.
Adding a production project, layer or assembly is Reserved.
Changing persistence boundaries (e.g. multiple persistence contexts) or persistence technology is Reserved.
Adding an infrastructure category (messaging, background processing, distributed cache, search, external storage, external identity) is Reserved.
Adding a major library or framework, or replacing approved baseline technology, is Reserved.
Introducing a project-wide convention or abstraction that other code is expected to follow is Reserved.
A breaking public API change is Reserved.
Defining product behavior or tunable values that the product sources do not define is Reserved.
Do not escalate routine local decisions already constrained by the specification, the decision register, existing code or the standards.

For a Reserved choice raise a Decision Request through architecture-decision and do not implement it before approval; an explicit user instruction counts as approval, and the accepted decision must still be recorded through architecture-decision.
exceptions: Explicit user instruction counts as approval.

normative_action: When SPECIFICATION.md is non-empty it is the authoritative source for project-specific functional requirements and observable product behavior.

Must not silently weaken, contradict or materially extend specified behavior, and must not silently invent user-visible behavior, limits, defaults, restrictions or workflows, even when they seem reasonable.
When an omitted detail must be decided and materially affects observable product behavior, propose the smallest reasonable option and ask for approval.
Routine internal implementation choices that do not change observable behavior need no approval.

Observable string semantics (case sensitivity, collation, culture vs ordinal, normalization, trimming, uniqueness, lookup) are product behavior; when the product sources do not define them, choosing them requires approval.

Approved project-level tunable limits and defaults (maximum lengths, page sizes, retention periods, numeric thresholds) live in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md, which never overrides SPECIFICATION.md (owner of behavioral intent).
SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md must not contradict each other; if they appear to conflict, stop and ask which source must be corrected; never choose one silently.

Must not silently invent a tunable value that materially changes accepted input or observable behavior: propose it, obtain approval, record it in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md, then synchronize it (custom-settings).
Must not store secrets, environment-specific connection details, package versions, HTTP status codes, ports, migration identifiers or incidental implementation constants in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.
The simplest maintainable solution, with architectural complexity proportional to current requirements and no speculative abstractions.
Must not introduce frameworks, libraries, infrastructure or architectural patterns without a concrete current need.
Changes stay within the requested scope and preserve existing behavior unless the task or the approved specification requires a change.
exceptions: Task or approved specification requires change.

normative_action: Before implementing a questionable request name the concrete concern (duplication, poor cohesion, trigger or loading problems, context cost, architecture or policy conflict, unnecessary complexity) and propose an alternative; never silently rewrite or ignore the user's requirement.
Must not commit, push, merge, rebase, reset, force-push, delete branches or run any other repository-changing Git operation unless explicitly requested; requested operations follow git-workflow.
Parallel implementation work uses separate branches or worktrees; keep unrelated changes out of the current branch.

Each workflow owns its procedure, stop conditions and report shape; run the matching workflow instead of improvising (development-workflow for implementation, verify for completion, code-review/code-reviewer for review, build-fix for repairs, add-dependency, custom-settings, persistence-change, architecture-decision, project-structure, delivery-change, security-scan, git-workflow).

A security scan is an evidence-based static review, not a penetration test; state its limitations (runtime-only, infrastructure outside the repo, business-logic abuse, complex authorization bypass, deployment weaknesses, dynamic exploitation) in the report and flag security-sensitive workflows for threat modeling instead of claiming the scan proves them secure.

Report concrete risks evaluated in the context of actual exposure and behavior, not generic security advice; do not report mechanical pattern matches (e.g. ordinary ORM LINQ is not SQL injection) or invent exploitability the code does not establish.

Every security finding distinguishes confirmed evidence from items needing verification (labelled NEEDS VERIFICATION); severity comes from exploitability, reachability, impact and application context, never from a suspicious pattern, CVSS score or OWASP category alone; confirmed findings carry severity, location, title, evidence, risk, impact, smallest remediation and OWASP category when applicable.

The security review must not depend on a specific MCP server, agent, analyzer, commercial scanner or other external tool; tooling output is evidence to be checked against the code, not the sole authority.

Inspect which surfaces exist and skip irrelevant checks instead of reporting them as failures; a full pre-release or requested audit reviews all applicable layers, a targeted change focuses on the affected layers and expands when it crosses security boundaries.

Security layer status is PASS, FINDINGS, NOT APPLICABLE or NOT CHECKED — never PASS for an uninspected layer; the scan is complete only when applicable layers were inspected, findings have evidence, uncertain findings are labelled and limitations are stated.

Security remediation prefers the smallest secure change consistent with the architecture; do not recommend a new authentication system unnecessarily, custom cryptography, blanket encryption of all fields, [Authorize] on every action under a protecting global policy, security libraries merely to satisfy the scan, or disabling functionality a scanner cannot understand; do not require security mechanisms the project does not need.

Swashbuckle Swagger UI (Swashbuckle.AspNetCore, configured in the Api/composition layer) is the Development interactive API documentation surface; the requirement is the interactive UI, not a standalone raw OpenAPI endpoint.

When API behavior changes verify controller behavior and relevant integration tests, verify response metadata, start the API when startup/composition changed, confirm the Development Swagger UI loads, exercise representative endpoints when meaningful, and preserve newly verified behavior in maintained tests.

Verification produces evidence that the requested change is complete without obvious regressions, at a depth matched to scope and risk, without requiring optional tooling the repository has not configured.

Before choosing any check review the final changed-file set and diff: changes match the requested scope with no unrelated refactoring, no accidental generated/build artifacts, no secrets or environment-specific credentials (remove any found); determine the affected areas (backend, frontend, both, documentation-only).

If an ad-hoc or manual behavioral probe uniquely demonstrated that the change works, the verified behavior must be represented by maintained automated test coverage before completion unless equivalent coverage exists (confirm it really exercises the behavior); temporary diagnostics/probes are removed only afterwards; builds, compilers, formatters, static analysis and existing suites need no new tests.
Build the affected solution/projects (frontend: the workspace's declared build script); avoid --no-restore unless restore is known complete; a build failure means the implementation is not complete.

Run tests covering the changed area (frontend: declared test script, no assumed runner); small solutions run the full suite, large ones affected projects then the broader suite required by risk; investigate every newly failing relevant test and never dismiss a failure as unrelated without checking.

For new runnable applications or substantial composition, startup, configuration, persistence or full-stack changes verify that the Development configuration actually starts (API host, Development endpoint, Swagger UI when exposed, configuration binding, database connectivity/initialization, frontend dev server, compatible API base URL and CORS); a successful build alone does not prove runtime composition.

Run architecture (standards + check-manifests; persistence-change incl. seeder when the model changed), co-change, formatting/analyzer (when configured, without adding tools just to verify), dependency and security checks (vulnerability inspection and changed secrets/authorization/raw SQL/CORS/TLS/logging/certificate validation) only when relevant to the change; a full security-scan is not required for every small change.

Review the final diff after all fixes for accidental unrelated edits, commented-out code, temporary logging, unintended TODO/FIXME markers, stale temporary tests or scripts, architecture drift, unapproved drift from SPECIFICATION.md or CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md, stale code/tests/docs/config after a settings change, and manually verified behavior never preserved as a test.

For every C# file created or modified by the task remove unused or redundant using directives (including those already provided by implicit/global usings unless needed for clarity or disambiguation) without unrelated repository-wide cleanup; verify the changed files rather than assuming tooling removed them.
exceptions: Usings kept for clarity or disambiguation.

normative_action: When verification fails identify the concrete failure, make the smallest appropriate fix, rerun the affected verification (and build/tests when code changed) and repeat until green or genuine user input is required; never hide a known failure and declare completion; persistent build/test failures go to build-fix.

Report what was actually run using PASS / NOT RUN / NOT APPLICABLE for backend build, frontend build, tests, runtime smoke, architecture/manifests, formatting, security/dependency checks and diff review, plus open Decision Requests; never imply that an unchecked area passed.

Repository-wide formatting and C# style configuration: UTF-8, space indentation (4; 2 for JSON/YAML/props/csproj/slnx/XML and web files), final newline, trailing-whitespace trimming (not for Markdown); file-scoped namespaces (suggestion), System usings first, unused-usings IDE0005 as suggestion; var when the type is apparent; modern language features, braces when multiline, expression bodies; PascalCase types/members, I-prefixed interfaces, Async suffix on async methods (silent).
trigger_scope: Editors and dotnet format for repository files
exceptions: Severities are suggestion/silent: style findings do not fail builds.

normative_action: Shared build configuration targets net10.0 for every .NET project below the repository root (Directory.Build.props holds genuinely shared settings only).
Shared build configuration enables Nullable reference types and ImplicitUsings for every .NET project below the repository root.
exceptions: Projects may override in their own files.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-023 says where shared settings live but no oracle policy chooses nullable reference types or implicit usings; the template makes both effective defaults for all projects.

normative_action: Not adopted: CQRS handlers, MediatR, Kommand, Vertical Slice Architecture or similar mediator-based organization; introducing any of them requires explicit approval.

Default persistence is EF Core with Microsoft SQL Server (Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer); provider-specific concerns stay out of Application and Domain; migration mechanism EF Core migrations; seeding mechanism a dedicated Development seeder.
Backend testing uses NUnit with test projects beside production projects under backend/; WebApplicationFactory<Program> is the ASP.NET Core integration-test baseline; Testcontainers is conditional.
Frontend stack: current stable Angular with compatible TypeScript/RxJS, standalone APIs, strict mode, routing, zoneless mode when supported, SCSS, Angular Material/CDK and Vitest.
Not added by default: NgRx, Axios, Lodash, Bootstrap, Tailwind or additional form/component/state libraries; use built-in Angular capabilities first and add extras only for a concrete need.
Use the approved technology; must not silently select an alternative; replacing approved technology requires approval.
Backend platform: .NET 10 LTS, C# 14, ASP.NET Core and ASP.NET Core Controllers; moving to a preview/RC release requires approval.
FluentValidation is the standard explicit request/use-case validation library; application code logs through ILogger<T> with Serilog as the logging provider.
Default layout: production and backend test projects in backend/<Name>.<Layer>/, the frontend workspace in frontend/<Name>.Web/, documentation in docs/; no separate top-level tests/ directory.
